findings.title: Distinct evidence labels do not prove independent observations
attack_path: A producer records one deterministic failure three times with different evidence labels.
The source reaches the occurrence and distinct-label thresholds.
The advisor can block a closely analogous plan.
evidence: Failure evidence references are mandatory and deduplicated but are not authenticated run receipts.
findings.recommendation: Require verified execution receipt identities before allowing broader scope or higher-impact consumers.

findings.title: Global negative procedures are refused
attack_path: A global failure record accumulates repeated evidence.
A derived rule could affect unrelated projects.
The assessor rejects it because cross-scope support is unavailable.
evidence: Ordinary weighted failure retrieval remains available.
findings.recommendation: Preserve refusal until a bounded cross-scope evidence contract is implemented and reviewed.

findings.title: Negative procedures cannot execute or become skills
attack_path: A malicious avoidance rule is stored in failure evidence.
No install, activation, tool, shell, network, or memory-write path exists in the projection.
evidence: The implementation creates no registry or persistence table.
findings.recommendation: Treat any future promotion bridge as a separate security-sensitive feature.

findings.title: The operator report exposes bounded failure guidance
attack_path: A caller with local database access requests an assessment.
The report includes failed action, environment, and avoidance rule.
Sensitive content previously stored in those fields becomes visible.
evidence: Failure creation already applies secret checks to structured environment and field-size bounds.
The CLI is local and read-only.
findings.recommendation: Continue avoiding secrets in failure text and rely on host database access controls.

limitations: This review does not authenticate historical evidence producers.
It does not establish that three observations are statistically sufficient outside the exact scope.
Host filesystem permissions govern access to failure content.
